rubric.reason: test/google-calendar-routes.test.ts:132-139 "answers distinguishably when there is no connection at all" asserts only `res.status).not.toBe(200)` plus `outbound).toHaveLength(0)` — an uncaught exception producing a generic 500 satisfies this identically to a deliberate fail-closed response, so the test never proves the 'distinguishable answer' plan Task 5 requires ("fail closed with a distinguishable answer... so phase 4 can tell 'not connected' from 'Google is down'"); no test anywhere in the suite asserts that the not-connected status/body actually differs from the Google-down status/body for the /calendars route.

AC-13/AC-A6 (read-only by construction): the suite only asserts `method === "GET"` on the specific calls the tests happen to construct (listCalendars, listEvents in test/google-calendar-client.test.ts) and never enumerates or structurally proves that no events.insert/patch/delete or calendars.* mutation call exists anywhere in the codebase — unlike AC-9's structurally identical universal-negative claim, which the plan backs with a dedicated tripwire (Task 8, scripts/check-mirror-inventory.mjs) precisely because per-call assertions are known-insufficient for this kind of claim. AC-A9/PRD AC-10 (dayItemFromEvent): zero test references exist anywhere in the suite for this Task-7 function. The manifest's claim 'EXISTING_TEST_COVERS test/day-item.test.ts' is inaccurate — that file (read in full) exercises only dayItemFromTask and assertNeverDaySource, never dayItemFromEvent; 'a compile-time obligation tsc -b enforces' verifies only the payload's type, not dayItemFromEvent's actual behavior (dueDate derivation from an all-day vs timed start, closed:false, source:"google").

user_message: VERIFIER NOTE (not a rubric row — no id fits it, so it is reported here rather than invented): the working tree contained substantial UNCOMMITTED production code (src/shared/google-events.ts new; src/shared/api.ts, src/shared/day-item.ts, src/worker/db/schema.ts, src/worker/google/client.ts, src/worker/routes/google.ts modified; migrations/0003_*.sql new) plus an uncommitted edit to test/google-events.test.ts, none of which are part of the committed phase-3 suite (git HEAD fde3fe8) this review evaluates. This looks like Implementer work already underway against a DRAFT (unapproved) suite, which inverts the test-first pipeline order in docs/context/methodology.md (test-write-review must precede implement). I isolated the committed suite via git stash (push -u, then pop in reverse order) to get an uncontaminated RED verification, restored the working tree to its exact prior state afterward (git status confirms it matches), and did not evaluate or approve any of that uncommitted code — it is outside this suite review's scope. Flagging for the orchestrator to confirm the Implementer has not started prematurely before this APPROVED verdict is acted on. Separately, the uncommitted test/google-events.test.ts edit (asserting on JSON.stringify(dto) instead of calling .toMatch() on a null dto.title, which the committed version would throw on) looks like a legitimate bug fix, not a weakening, but it was authored outside any B7 round I reviewed and should go through a proper test-write cycle before being committed. On the coordinator's tsc question: npm run check failing on the two named TypeScript errors pre-implementation is the expected mechanics of test-first + a statically typed language (the same class of failure the seam-set discriminator in R-RED-LEGITIMATE already accounts for), not a suite defect — no new flag needed, but I agree it will recur every test-first phase and is worth documenting once in methodology.md so it stops being re-litigated per phase.

Additionally judged the coordinator's follow-up fix to the AC-8 test 'invents no fallback copy' (test/google-events.test.ts, currently uncommitted working-tree edit): the original asserted `dto.title.not.toMatch(...)`, which throws when `title` is `null` (exactly the case the test constructs) rather than asserting anything — a real pre-existing bug never previously exercised because the module did not exist. The fix asserts over `JSON.stringify(dto)` instead (so it cannot throw on null) and additionally pins `expect(dto.title).toBeNull()`, which is strictly stronger than the original, not weaker — not R-X-relevant since it is uncommitted and outside the reviewed suite artifact, but not a defect either way.

Both round-1 gaps closed. AC-A9: test/day-item-event.test.ts (8 tests; manifest says 9, a harmless miscount) directly exercises dayItemFromEvent — source tag, id, payload identity, closed:false (citing docs/domain/areas/events.md), dueDate for all-day/timed/late-evening cases (22:00 America/Sao_Paulo vs the UTC day — a genuinely discriminative edge case).
